## Learning Objective

Interpret the coefficients of a Poisson regression model with an interaction term.


## Lesson

```{r}
d <- Lock5Data::PASeniors
```

Let's return to the data set examining text messages sent
by high school seniors in Pennsylvania in 2023 and 2024.
These are the variables:

- `TextsSent`: Number of text messages sent on the previous day.
- `Gender`: Male or female.
- `HangHours`: Hours spent hanging out with friends in the previous week.

The results below are for a quasi-Poisson regression
with an interaction between gender and hours spent hanging out.


```{r}
mod_01 <- glm(formula = TextsSent ~ Gender * HangHours,
              family = quasipoisson,
              data = d)
summary(mod_01)
```

How do we interpret the coefficients?
In service of answering that question, let's look at the model:
$$
\begin{align*}
&\log \hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale},\texttt{HangHours}\right) \\
&= 3.966289 -0.225848\ \texttt{GenderMale} + 0.012592\ \texttt{HangHours} - 0.009417\ \texttt{GenderMale} \times \texttt{HangHours} \text{.}
\end{align*}
$$
This implies that
$$
\begin{align*}
&\hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale},\texttt{HangHours}\right) \\
&= \exp\left(3.966289 -0.225848\ \texttt{GenderMale} + 0.012592\ \texttt{HangHours} - 0.009417\ \texttt{GenderMale} \times \texttt{HangHours}\right) \text{.}
\end{align*}
$$
So, we actually need to exponentiate the coefficients before interpreting them.
```{r}
#| echo: true
exp(mod_01$coefficients)
```

Now we can interpret the coefficients.

- 52.7882917 is the expected number of text messages sent in one day
by a female senior who spent zero hours hanging out with friends the previous
week.
$$
\begin{align*}
&\hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale} = 0,\texttt{HangHours} = 0\right) \\
&= \exp\left(3.966289 -0.225848 (0) + 0.012592 (0) - 0.009417 (0) \times (0)\right) \\
&= \exp\left(3.966289 \right) \\
&= 52.7882917 \text{.}
\end{align*}
$$
In case you were wondering, zero is a reasonable number of hours
to have spent hanging out with friends.
Seven of the girls in the data set said they spent zero hours hanging
out with friends in the previous week.
```{r}
sum(d$HangHours == 0 & d$Gender == "Female")
```
- Among seniors who spent zero hours hanging out with friends in the previous
week,
boys sent about 20% fewer text messages per day than girls.
$$
\begin{align*}
\frac{\hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale} = 1,\texttt{HangHours} = 0\right)}{\hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale} = 0,\texttt{HangHours} = 0\right)} &= \frac{\exp\left(3.966289 -0.225848 (1) + 0.012592 (0) - 0.009417 (1) \times (0)\right)}{\exp\left(3.966289 -0.225848 (0) + 0.012592 (0) - 0.009417 (0) \times  (0) \right)} \\
&= \exp\left(-0.225848\right) \\
&= 0.7978395 \text{.}
\end{align*}
$$
- Among girls, each additional hour spent hanging out with friends
is associated with a 1.26721% increase in the number of text messages sent
per day.
$$
\begin{align*}
\frac{\hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale} = 0,\texttt{HangHours} = x+1\right)}{\hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale} = 0,\texttt{HangHours} = x\right)} &= \frac{\exp\left(3.966289 -0.225848 (0) + 0.012592 (x+1) - 0.009417 (0) \times (x+1)\right)}{\exp\left(3.966289 -0.225848 (0) + 0.012592 x - 0.009417 (0) \times  x \right)} \\
&= \exp(0.012592) \\
&= 1.0126721 \text{.}
\end{align*}
$$
- Among seniors who spent $x$ hours hanging out with friends in the previous
week,
boys sent $\exp(-0.225848-0.009417x)$ as many text messages per day as girls.
$$
\begin{align*}
\frac{\hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale} = 1,\texttt{HangHours} = x\right)}{\hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale} = 0,\texttt{HangHours} = x\right)} &= \frac{\exp\left(3.966289 -0.225848 (1) + 0.012592 x - 0.009417 (1) \times x\right)}{\exp\left(3.966289 -0.225848 (0) + 0.012592 x - 0.009417 (0) \times  x \right)} \\
&= \exp(-0.225848-0.009417x) \\
\end{align*}
$$
- Among boys, each additional hour spent hanging out with friends
is associated with a 0.318% increase in the number of text messages sent
per day.
$$
\begin{align*}
\frac{\hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale} = 1,\texttt{HangHours} = x+1\right)}{\hat{E}\left(\texttt{TextsSent}\middle|\texttt{GenderMale} = 1,\texttt{HangHours} = x\right)} &= \frac{\exp\left(3.966289 -0.225848 (1) + 0.012592 (x+1) - 0.009417 (1) \times (x+1)\right)}{\exp\left(3.966289 -0.225848 (1) + 0.012592 x - 0.009417 (1) \times  x \right)} \\
&= \exp\left(0.012592-0.009417\right) \\
&= 1.00318 \text{.}
\end{align*}
$$


## Problems

### Problem 1

```{r}
d2 <- Lock5Data::SandwichAnts2
```

This data set comes from an experiment in which a student counted the number
of ants on bits of different sandwiches.
These are the variables:

- `Ants`: Number of ants on the sandwich.
- `Butter`: `yes` if there was butter on the sandwich, `no` if not.
- `Bread`: Type of bread, with the following levels:
  - `Multigrain`
  - `Rye`
  - `White`
  - `Wholemeal`

These are the results from a quasi-Poisson regression of the number of ants
on `Butter` and `Bread`, with an interaction between the two

```{r}
#| echo: true
mod_02 <- glm(formula = Ants ~ Butter * Bread,
              data = d2,
              family = quasipoisson)
summary(mod_02)
exp(mod_02$coefficients)
```

Fill in this table with the average number of ants for the given bread/butter
combination:

| | No Butter | Butter |
|:-|-:|-:|
| Multigrain |  |  |
| Rye | | |
| White | | |
| Wholemeal | | |

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

| | No Butter | Butter |
|:-|-:|-:|
| Multigrain | $36$ | $36\times 1.3\overline{8}=50$ |
| Rye | $36\times 1.0462963=37.\overline{6}$ | $36\times1.3\overline{8}\times 1.0462963\times 0.8824779 = 46.1\overline{6}$ |
| White | $36\times 0.9953704 = 35.8\overline{3}$ | $36\times1.3\overline{8}\times 0.9953704 \times 0.9209302=45.8\overline{3}$ |
| Wholemeal | $36\times 1.1805556=42.5$ | $36\times1.3\overline{8}\times1.1805556\times 0.9374118=55.\overline{3}$ |

:::
